title: Deferred Onboarding and Role Reskilling Playbook (Bridge Program)
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Summary: This playbook documents the accepted process for managing hires or internal transfers who start later than their original start date (deferred starts) and the structured reskilling pathways (Bridge Program) for employees who change roles and require a focused ramp. It combines People Ops operational tasks, manager responsibilities, expected timelines, and metrics to minimize time-to-impact while protecting candidate experience and compliance.

Scope
- Applies to: new hires with confirmed but delayed start dates, accepted offers where the candidate requests a deferral (>2 weeks), and internal transfers that require reskilling (>3 weeks of formal training).
- Not in scope: short reschedules under 2 business days, contractors with ad-hoc start windows, apprenticeship/returnship special programs (see related pages).

Goals
- Maintain candidate/employee engagement during deferral windows.
- Provide repeatable manager/People Ops steps to re-onboard or bridge skills.
- Target median time-to-competency: 8 weeks for lateral transfers, 12 weeks for role transitions with new technical domains.
- Reduce churn during pre-start and early employment by 50% vs ad-hoc approaches.

Definitions
- Deferred Start: an accepted offer with a confirmed start date > 2 weeks after offer acceptance.
- Bridge Program: a targeted, time-bound reskilling curriculum for employees changing role families or adding new core competencies.
- Reskilling Path: curated set of courses, mentors, shadow tasks, and evaluation gates to certify readiness.

Principles
- Candidate-centric: prioritize transparent comms and predictable checkpoints.
- Manager accountability: manager owns role-specific curriculum and success criteria.
- People Ops partnership: People Ops owns program templates, compliance, and reporting.
- Measured ramp: use objective checkpoints (skills checks, paired sessions, feature contributions).

Roles & Ownership
- Hiring Manager: defines technical and behavioral competency gates; assigns mentor and initial project.
- People Ops Lead (onboarding specialist): confirms schedule, maintains pre-start comm cadence, provisions access, and manages legal/comp paperwork timelines.
- Learning & Development (L&D): curates learning modules and schedules cohort sessions.
- Mentor (peer): provides weekly 1:1 for first 8 weeks of ramp.
- IT/Security: completes device, network, and role-based access setup no later than 3 business days before actual start.

Deferred-Start Playbook (People Ops + Hiring Manager)
1) At offer acceptance (Day 0)
   - Capture preferred start window and any planned deferred dates in Workday/HRIS.
   - Set expected timeline expectations in offer email: include sample pre-start comm cadence.
   - People Ops: schedule one formal check-in 2 weeks before proposed start and an optional weekly update for longer deferrals (>6 weeks).

2) If candidate requests deferral before signature
   - Treat as negotiation: update offer terms, confirm final start date, reissue paperwork, and update recruiter/finance.

3) For confirmed deferral (>2 weeks) after signature
   - People Ops tasks (timeline):
     - Day 1 (post-confirmation): create Deferred Onboarding record, notify IT and Security.
     - Weekly: short status email to candidate (one paragraph) with 2–3 highlights about team and product.
     - T-minus 21 days before start: confirm equipment timeline, training plan, and 1:1 schedule with manager.
     - T-minus 3 business days: tech access provisioning and calendar invites for Day 1.

4) Pre-start engagement (recommended cadence)
   - 6–8 weeks out (if deferral is long): invite to optional monthly Product Office Hours and shared learning channels.
   - 2–3 weeks out: send Welcome Guide (high level org map, first-week agenda, pre-work).
   - 2–3 business days out: final logistics email (parking/remote links, Slack invite, hardware delivery windows).

5) Day 1 adjustments (for deferred starts)
   - Manager to run a tailored 90-minute immersion rather than standard 30–60 minute check-in.
   - Assign 30-day objectives that are realistic given deferral.

Bridge Program: Role Reskilling Process (internal transfers or hires needing skills bridge)
- Program length banding by scope:
  - Minor reskill (tooling or process change, <2 new competencies): 4–6 weeks.
  - Moderate reskill (new framework/team conventions, 2–4 competencies): 8–12 weeks.
  - Major reskill (different discipline, e.g., infra -> model-serving, >4 competencies): 12–16 weeks.

- Standard Bridge program components (template):
  - Week-by-week learning plan with milestone outcomes.
  - Assigned mentor and owner of weekly tasks.
  - Sprint-style project: small scoped deliverable to demonstrate applied learning (typically delivered by week 6–8).
  - Formal competency check at program mid-point and end (skill rubric).
  - 1:1 cadence: weekly for first 12 weeks, then biweekly until certification.

Example Training Matrix (use as template)
| Competency | Learning Assets | Hands-on Tasks | Cert Gate | Owner | Target Week |
|------------|-----------------|----------------|----------|-------|-------------|
| Core infra patterns | internal wiki, 2-hour workshop | shadow deploy + runbook update | review PR + runbook | Manager | 1–4 |
| Model-serving basics | L&D course, external reading | local inference test + perf summary | evaluation quiz + demo | Mentor | 2–6 |
| Observability and SLOs | dashboard walkthroughs | build one alert + dashboard | peer review | SRE partner | 4–8 |

Manager Checklist (Pre-start and Weeks 0–12)
- Pre-start (T-minus 21d): confirm mentor, first sprint, and access.
- Day 1: 90-minute immersion, calendar and expectation alignment.
- Week 1: set 30/60/90 objectives and small first deliverable.
- Week 2–4: weekly 1:1, confirm hands-on tasks and pair sessions.
- Week 6: mid-program checkpoint (objective evidence review + rubric scoring).
- Week 12: final certification meeting and plan next steps (stretch assignments, recurring mentoring cadence).

People Ops / L&D Checklist
- Create Deferred Onboarding record and enable pre-start comms.
- Reserve cohort space in L&D calendar (if curriculum required).
- Track access ticket age; escalate to SOC/IT owner after 48 hours.
- Log program enrollments for quarterly Bridge Program reporting.

Templates & Example Messages
- Pre-start check-in (2 weeks out):
  "Hi <Candidate Name>, hope you're well — just checking in ahead of your start on <Start Date>. We've scheduled your first-day agenda and have updated the equipment plan. Let me know if anything has changed; otherwise we'll connect again one week before. — <People Ops Rep>"

- Manager Day 1 invitation (subject): "Welcome + 90-minute immersion: practical first steps"
  Body: short agenda, 1:1 mentor intro, and first sprint description.

Evaluation & Metrics
- Primary KPIs (tracked quarterly):
  - Median time-to-competency (weeks to hit objective gate): target 8–12 weeks depending on banding.
  - Pre-start engagement rate: % candidates responding to at least one pre-start comm in last 4 weeks (target > 80%).
  - Equipment/access SLA: % of hires with full access by Day 0 (target 95%).
  - Deferred-start churn: % of deferred hires who do not start (target < 4%).

Escalation & Exceptions
- If access is not provisioned by T-minus 3 business days: People Ops escalates to IT lead and copies Security.
- If candidate requests second deferral: treat as re-negotiation and require manager+People Ops approval; document changes in offer record.
- If mid-program competency score < 60% at mid-point: extend bridge by 2–4 weeks with revised milestone and L&D support.

Recordkeeping & Reporting
- Store deferred-start notes in HRIS under candidate record and tag with "deferred-bridge" label.
- People Ops to publish quarterly Bridge Program summary: enrollment, pass rate, average time-to-certification, and any action items.

Related Pages & Resources
- Returnship and internal mobility guidelines (see related_pages).
- Onboarding immersion rotation playbook for Day 1 templates.
- L&D course catalog (internal link).

Appendices
A. Sample 8-week Bridge program outline (week-by-week bullets):
- Week 1: orientation, pairing, small hands-on ticket.
- Week 2: core concept deep dive, automated test + PR.
- Week 3: mini-project planning.
- Week 4: mid-program review + rubric feedback.
- Week 5–6: project execution, demos.
- Week 7: stabilization and cross-team shadow.
- Week 8: final demo, competency certification, next assignment.

B. Suggested rubric dimensions (score 0–5 each):
- Technical correctness, independent delivery, code quality, system understanding, observability contributions, communication.

C. FAQ (short)
- Q: Can a deferred start be lengthened twice?
  A: Only with Manager + People Ops approval; third deferral triggers review by Head of Talent.

- Q: Who pays for equipment delays?
  A: Redwood covers shipping and standard hardware; exceptions require finance approval.

Versioning & Ownership
- Owner: People Ops (Onboarding Specialist team)
- Last reviewed: 2026-02-14
- Review cadence: annual or after any material change to onboarding or HRIS flows.
